title: Forward copy of opaque 36-byte records
summary: Recovered VA 0x422580 using original disassembly and its vector reallocation caller at 0x422491. Copies each record in ordered 16/16/4-byte chunks, checks output for null on each iteration, advances both addresses by 36, and leaves the final output address in EAX. Portable API replaces the private ECX/EDX plus caller-cleaned stack ABI; the test oracle uses GCC regparm(3) with an ignored EAX argument.
test_description: Direct original comparison for 0 through 8 records, all 16 source alignments and varied destination alignments, identical ranges and partial overlaps in both directions with offsets 0 through 40. Compares final EAX address offset and all 640 buffer bytes, including source and surrounding guards. Tests empty null range and a single skipped null-output record with unreadable source. Installs initialized FS storage and checks restoration after every oracle call.
known_limits: Record field meanings are unknown; only its 36-byte opaque layout is established.
Malformed ranges that never reach end, address-space wrapping, and faulting accesses are not executed in tests. Null output with multiple records advances to address 36 and would normally fault.
Implementation uses SSE2 intrinsics for original transfer ordering; other architecture ports need equivalent ordered chunk snapshots.
The original caller ignores EAX; the exposed return preserves its observed final destination address without claiming an original source-level return type.
No byte matching claim; caller allocation and vector ownership logic are outside scope.
